territory: Cross-cutting lens: Vercel platform limits — 4.5MB request/response body cap, function duration ceilings, after()/waitUntil fire-and-forget survival, module-scope init, streaming-then-error — audited across all 14 API routes, all upload client paths, the email queue, retention sweep/account purge, catch-up advance, the (main) layout, proxy.ts, and the storage/rate-limit/prisma/email/image lib layer.

findings.title: Onboarding photo step ships the raw file (up to 15MB) through a Server Action; anything over ~4.5MB dies at Vercel's platform body cap with no error shown and the button stuck on busy
findings.expected: A new member uploading a normal 5-12MB phone photo during onboarding either succeeds (via crop/downscale so the wire bytes are small) or sees a clear error.
findings.actual: The step validates only `if (file.size > 15 * 1024 * 1024)` and then sends the ORIGINAL bytes: `const fd = new FormData(); fd.set("file", file); const result = await updateAvatar(fd);`. Server Actions are Vercel function invocations, hard-capped at ~4.5MB request body regardless of next.config's `serverActions.bodySizeLimit: "25mb"`. The platform answers 413 before the action runs, the awaited action call rejects, and `handlePick` has NO try/catch — so the rejection is unhandled, `setBusy(false)` never runs, and the member stares at a permanently busy button with no toast. Any photo between 4.5MB and 15MB (most phone photos) reproduces it.
findings.evidence: photo-step.tsx handlePick: `if (file.size > 15 * 1024 * 1024) { toast.error("Photo must be under 15MB"); return; } setBusy(true); const fd = new FormData(); fd.set("file", file); const result = await updateAvatar(fd); setBusy(false);` — no try/catch, no crop, no downscale. The codebase itself documents this exact failure mode as a bug it fixed elsewhere: letterhead-profile.tsx:363-366 "the old path shipped the ORIGINAL bytes to a hard-coded centre crop... a 6MB phone photo could die on Vercel's ~4.5MB serverless body cap" — the profile surface got the crop-dialog fix (uploads a tiny 512px WebP blob), the onboarding surface did not. The presign route's own comment (upload/presign/route.ts:11-13) confirms the platform cap: "Vercel caps serverless request bodies at ~4.5MB no matter what bodySizeLimit says".
findings.fixDirection: Reuse the existing avatar crop dialog (src/components/settings/avatar-crop-dialog.tsx, outputs a 512px WebP well under the cap) in the onboarding photo step, exactly as letterhead-profile.tsx does; at minimum run downscaleImage() from src/lib/image-downscale.ts before building the FormData, and wrap the `await updateAvatar(fd)` in try/catch that resets busy and toasts.
findings.gateOrTest: New e2e/manual check: onboarding photo step with a >4.5MB fixture image against a production build; assert an error toast appears and the button re-enables. A unit test on the step's handler asserting the file handed to updateAvatar is <4.5MB.
findings.reproPlan: Test-account write via the app UI on the production deployment: sign up a throwaway account, reach the onboarding photo step, pick a 6MB JPEG, observe the hang and the 413 in the network tab.

findings.title: Catch-up answer photos allow 5MB per file and 3 files in ONE request to /api/upload — both over Vercel's 4.5MB total body cap, failing with a 'try again' toast that can never succeed
findings.expected: A photo the client-side check accepts should be uploadable in production; multi-file batches should respect the total request-size ceiling.
findings.actual: `const MAX_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024;` (5,242,880) is ABOVE Vercel's ~4.5MB (4,718,592) function body cap, so a single 4.6-5MB photo passes the client check and dies at the platform edge. Worse, the check is per-file while all picked files go in one request: `picked.forEach((file) => formData.append("files", file)); const res = await fetch("/api/upload", ...)` — three 3MB photos (9MB total, each individually 'valid') also die. The platform's 413 body is not JSON, so `await res.json()` throws, landing in the catch: `toast.error("That photo would not upload. Try again.")` — permanent condition presented as transient. There is no presign path and no downscale on this surface (header comment: "Uploads through POST /api/upload").
findings.evidence: photo-attachments.tsx:24 `const MAX_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024;`; lines 50-54 check `file.size > MAX_BYTES` per file only; lines 58-62 append every picked file to one FormData and POST once. Compare src/lib/image-downscale.ts:4-9 which exists precisely because "on Vercel a route handler's request body is hard-capped at about 4.5MB... a normal phone photo (often 5 to 12MB) sailed past the client check and then died at Vercel's edge with an opaque failure" — the feed composer got that fix, this surface did not.
findings.fixDirection: Run downscaleImage() on each picked file before appending (2048px WebP output is far under the cap even ×3), or upload files one-per-request like create-post-form's sequential loop, or move this surface onto the shared directUploadPut presign path. Also lower/align the client MAX_BYTES message with what production actually accepts.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test asserting the combined FormData payload for the max allowed batch stays under 4.5MB; manual: attach a 4.8MB photo to a Catch-up answer on production.
findings.reproPlan: Test-account write via the app UI: open a Catch-up answer, attach a 4.8MB JPEG, watch the 413 in the network tab and the misleading toast.

findings.title: purgeUserAccount deletes R2 objects one at a time after the DB rows are already gone; a duration-ceiling timeout mid-loop permanently orphans a purged member's publicly-fetchable images, and the retention sweep multiplies the exposure by running every due purge in one invocation
findings.expected: Account purge (GDPR Art. 17, audits H9/M35) removes all of a member's stored images even for a prolific account, and survives a function timeout resumably.
findings.actual: account-purge.ts:99-102 first commits `prisma.$transaction([report.deleteMany, user.delete])` — cascading away every row that points at the images — then loops `for (const url of urls) { await delImage(url); deleted += 1; }` sequentially. MAX_PHOTOS_PER_ACCOUNT is 1000 and each Photo carries 2-3 objects (thumbUrl, url, originalUrl) plus post/catch-up images, so a heavy account is hundreds to thousands of sequential DeleteObject round-trips at ~50-300ms each — minutes of runtime. No maxDuration is configured anywhere (vercel.json sets only regions+crons; no route exports maxDuration), so the deploy rides the platform default (300s Fluid / 60s legacy Hobby). On timeout: the user row is gone (transaction committed), the remaining R2 URLs exist nowhere ("the cascade takes the pointing rows with it and afterwards nothing can enumerate the objects" — the file's own comment), so those images stay publicly fetchable at their pub-*.r2.dev URLs forever — the exact H9 failure mode the function exists to close. The retention sweep (retention.ts:120-135) runs EVERY due account's purge inside one function invocation, so a wave of deletions maturing on the same night compounds it, and a timeout also skips the sweep's final `writeAudit` (retention.ts:151), leaving no record the sweep ran. adminDeleteUser (admin-actions.ts:59) awaits the same loop inside a Server Action, so deleting a prolific member can time out and show the admin an error although the row delete succeeded. Bonus defect: `deleted += 1` counts every attempt because delImage swallows failures, so the audit line "N stored image(s) removed" records attempts, not deletions.
findings.evidence: account-purge.ts:108-113: `let deleted = 0; for (const url of urls) { await delImage(url); deleted += 1; } return { ok: true, imagesDeleted: deleted };` — sequential, unbatched, post-commit. account-purge.ts:78-80 comment: "URLs are collected FIRST, because the cascade takes the pointing rows with it and afterwards nothing can enumerate the objects" — which is precisely why a mid-loop death is unrecoverable. upload-shared.ts:21 `MAX_PHOTOS_PER_ACCOUNT = 1000`. vercel.json contains no functions/maxDuration block; grep for maxDuration across src returns nothing.
findings.fixDirection: Batch the deletes with S3 DeleteObjectsCommand (R2 supports up to 1000 keys per call) or chunked Promise.all; and make the purge resumable by persisting the collected URL list (e.g. a PurgeQueue row written in the same transaction as the user delete) that the nightly sweep drains and retries, so a timeout loses nothing. Cap purges-per-sweep-invocation. Count only successful deletes (have delImage report success) in imagesDeleted. Consider an explicit `export const maxDuration` on /api/retention/sweep.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on a refactored purge that asserts object deletion is batched and that an injected failure leaves a resumable record; the existing audit entry should assert real deletions.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (any live proof deletes real member data).

findings.title: All three telemetry writers (recordLoginAttempt, logSearch, recordView) are floating promises with no after() wrapper — the writes die non-deterministically once the response is sent on Vercel
findings.expected: Post-response bookkeeping on Vercel must be registered via after()/waitUntil (the codebase's own established pattern: layout.tsx:63, feed/actions.ts:180, email-queue.ts:373) or it is not guaranteed to execute.
findings.actual: recordLoginAttempt fires `void prisma.loginAttempt.create(...).catch(...)` (login-attempt.ts:46) and is called synchronously seven times in auth.ts's authorize; the credentials route responds the moment authorize returns, racing the insert against the instance freeze. users/search:72 and places/search:127 do `void logSearch({...})` immediately before `return NextResponse.json(...)`. The four content pages do `void recordView(...)` during render. None are inside after(). Consequence in production only: LoginAttempt rows (the audit-H4/H6 'who cannot sign in' admin panel — blocked members, rate-limited members), SearchLog rows and ContentView counters are silently lost at random, so the owner's support and analytics surfaces undercount in a way dev never reproduces. The queue drain and collection copy already demonstrate the correct after() pattern in the same repo.
findings.evidence: login-attempt.ts:43-46: "Deliberately not awaited by the caller..." `void prisma.loginAttempt.create({...}).catch(...)`. users/search/route.ts:72: `void logSearch({ scope: "people", ... }); return NextResponse.json(users);`. profile/[id]/page.tsx:117: `void recordView(session.user.id, "profile", user.id);`. Contrast (main)/layout.tsx:63 `after(async () => { await drainMailQueue(); ... })` — the repo knows the rule; these nine call sites predate or missed it.
findings.fixDirection: Wrap each fire-and-forget in `after(() => ...)` from next/server (with the existing try/catch-throws fallback pattern scheduleDrain uses for non-request contexts, since authorize may run where after() throws). Behaviour for the member is unchanged; the write simply survives the response.
findings.gateOrTest: Extend src/lib/security-regressions.test.mjs (or a new unit test) to assert the call sites route through an after()-wrapping helper; live: compare LoginAttempt row count to attempted sign-ins on production over a day.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only-ish live proof: perform a failed sign-in and a people-search on production with a test account, then check (via admin analytics pages) whether rows appeared; repeat ~20x and count the shortfall.

findings.title: Message-to-admin composer uploads attachments with no client size check and no downscale; any image over ~4.5MB fails with 'Try again in a moment?' — a permanent condition presented as transient
findings.expected: The support-message screenshot flow should either shrink the image client-side (like the feed composer's fallback does via downscaleImage) or tell the member the file is too large.
findings.actual: handlePickImage builds FormData from the raw picked file and POSTs to /api/upload with no size validation at all: `const form = new FormData(); form.append("files", file); const res = await fetch("/api/upload", ...)`. The server route advertises a 20MB limit, but Vercel rejects >4.5MB bodies before the route runs; the 413 response is not JSON so `await res.json()` throws into the catch: `toast.error("That image didn't upload. Try again in a moment?")`. A member attaching a phone photo of a problem (5-12MB typical) retries forever. This is the support channel — the place members go when something is already wrong.
findings.evidence: message-composer.tsx:59-76: no reference to MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES, downscaleImage, or directUploadPut anywhere in the file; the only guard is the server's, which the platform cap pre-empts. image-downscale.ts:4-10 documents the identical failure mode this surface never received the fix for.
findings.fixDirection: Call downscaleImage(file) before building the FormData (screenshots compress extremely well), or reuse the presign path; add a client-side size check with an honest message as backstop.
findings.gateOrTest: Manual: attach a 6MB photo to a new admin message on production; unit test asserting the composer passes files through downscaleImage.
findings.reproPlan: Test-account write via the app UI: /messages, attach a 6MB JPEG, observe 413 + misleading toast.

findings.title: Collection contribute fallback sends the raw ≤20MB file through the contributePhoto Server Action without the browser downscale the post composer's fallback has — so whenever presign is unavailable (preview URL, new domain, transient failure), photos over 4.5MB fail permanently for no benefit
findings.expected: When the direct-to-R2 path is unavailable, the fallback should still be able to deliver the photo — as the post composer's fallback does by downscaling first (create-post-form.tsx:394 `const shrunk = await downscaleImage(original); return uploadOneFile(shrunk);`).
findings.actual: contribute-dialog.tsx:134-144: on `staged === null` it does `fd.set("file", file)` with the ORIGINAL file and calls `contributePhoto(fd)` — a Server Action, capped at ~4.5MB on Vercel, so any real phone photo or scan >4.5MB fails every time on any origin the R2 CORS allowlist does not name (upload-client.ts:11-12 names "a new domain, a Vercel preview URL" as expected triggers, and any transient presign failure also returns null). The 'full resolution is the point' rationale does not apply here: contributePhoto itself re-encodes to 1600px WebP (collection/actions.ts:170-174), so a 2048px browser downscale before the fallback would lose essentially nothing while making the fallback actually work. The catch shows the generic "may be too large, or the connection dropped. Try again." toast — retry can never succeed.
findings.evidence: contribute-dialog.tsx:135-144 builds FormData from `file` (the raw pick, validated only ≤20MB at pickFile:93) with no downscaleImage import anywhere in the file; create-post-form.tsx:394 shows the sibling surface applying `downscaleImage` in exactly this fallback; collection/actions.ts:170 `.resize(1600, 1600, { fit: "inside" ...})` proves the server discards resolution above 1600px on this path anyway.
findings.fixDirection: In the `staged === null` branch, run downscaleImage(file) (2048px ceiling ≥ the server's 1600px output) before `fd.set("file", ...)`, mirroring create-post-form's fallback.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit/e2e: with directUploadPut stubbed to return null, assert the file handed to contributePhoto is under 4.5MB for a 10MB input.
findings.reproPlan: Live proof on a Vercel PREVIEW deployment (origin not in the R2 CORS allowlist): contribute a 6MB photo to the Collection with a test account; the direct PUT is CORS-blocked, the fallback 413s.

findings.title: For unconfirmed members, every authenticated page render blocks on a synchronous Resend API call with no timeout — a slow or down email provider turns their whole app into hung pages
findings.expected: A page render should not be held hostage by a third-party mail API; provider slowness should degrade to the 'imminent' banner state, not to a hanging page.
findings.actual: layout.tsx:44-46 awaits `verificationMailState(session.user.id)` inside the render-blocking Promise.all for every unconfirmed member. email-queue.ts:597-599: when their verify row is queued and budget remains, it calls `await claimAndSend(row)` synchronously — which awaits `sendMail` → `api.emails.send(...)` (email.ts:181), a network call with no AbortController/timeout anywhere in the chain. The design intent ("one Resend call inside one page load, once") holds only while Resend answers promptly; if Resend hangs (chaos row: email provider down mid-signup — exactly when unconfirmed members exist in numbers, i.e. launch day), each such member's page views hang until the provider responds or the function duration ceiling 504s the page. The daily budget check does not protect against latency, only volume.
findings.evidence: layout.tsx:44-46: `session.user.emailConfirmed ? Promise.resolve(null) : verificationMailState(session.user.id)` inside `await Promise.all([...])`. email-queue.ts:594-599: "Budget is available, so nothing may sit queued: send it now." `const outcome = await claimAndSend(row);`. email.ts:180-187: `await api.emails.send({...})` with no timeout configured; the Resend SDK does not impose one by default.
findings.fixDirection: Race the in-render send against a short timeout (~2-3s) and fall through to the honest 'imminent' state on expiry (the row stays claimed/queued and the after() drain retries it); or move the repair-send itself into after() and have the banner poll. Additionally give sendMail an AbortController timeout so no caller can hang on the provider.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on verificationMailState with a sendMail stub that never resolves, asserting the function returns 'imminent' within the timeout budget.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (requires making Resend hang; not reproducible safely against production).

findings.title: Abandoned presigned uploads leak R2 objects forever: a browser that PUTs to staging/ or collection/*-o.* but never calls finalize leaves up to 20MB per object with no lifecycle rule and no cleanup job
findings.expected: Staged originals that are never finalized (tab closed between PUT and finalize, network drop, browser crash) are eventually reclaimed — via an R2 lifecycle rule on the staging/ prefix or a periodic sweep.
findings.actual: The presign route mints keys under `staging/<uid>/...` (posts) and `collection/<uid>/...-o.*` (collection) and the browser PUTs directly to R2. Cleanup of the staged original happens only inside the finalize route's `finally { await delImageByKey(key); }` (finalize/route.ts:121-124) and contributePhotoDirect's success/error paths — i.e. only when the SECOND request actually arrives. Nothing else ever touches these prefixes: the retention sweep (retention.ts) is DB-rows-only, grep for 'staging' across src finds no sweep, and no doc records an R2 lifecycle rule (docs/OPERATIONS.md and docs/SECURITY.md have no mention). Each abandoned attempt strands up to 20MB; the uploads rate limit allows 40/hour/user, so flaky mobile sessions across 2,000 members accumulate real storage cost with no way to distinguish live from dead objects except age — which nothing checks.
findings.evidence: presign/route.ts:104-106 builds the staged key; finalize/route.ts:122-123 comment "The staged original's job is done either way" — but only executes when finalize is called. retention.ts contains only prisma deleteMany + purgeUserAccount; no S3 client import. keyForUrl/KNOWN_ROOTS include "staging" (storage.ts:63) yet no code path lists or expires that prefix.
findings.fixDirection: Add an R2 lifecycle rule (dashboard) expiring objects under staging/ after ~2 days and *-o.* collection originals after ~2 days (finalize deletes them in seconds when the flow completes); or add a step to the nightly retention sweep that lists the staging/ prefix and deletes objects older than 48h. Document it in docs/OPERATIONS.md either way.
findings.gateOrTest: Operational check in docs/OPERATIONS.md; optionally an admin panel counter of staging-prefix object count/age so growth is visible.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only live proof: presign an upload with a test account, PUT the object, never call finalize, confirm the object still exists at its public URL days later (HEAD request).

findings.title: Worst-case image finalize work (3×20MB originals; full-resolution q90 WebP encode up to 100MP) can exceed the function duration ceiling, and no route or vercel.json sets maxDuration so the deploy rides an unverified platform default
findings.expected: The heaviest legitimate upload (a large heritage scan near the 20MB/100MP limits, or three near-max post images in one finalize call) completes within the function's duration limit, or the limit is explicitly configured with headroom.
findings.actual: finalize/route.ts processes up to 3 keys sequentially, each: R2 HEAD + GET of ≤20MB + sharp decode (≤100MP allowed by MAX_INPUT_PIXELS, image.ts:24) + 1920px WebP encode + PUT + DELETE. contributePhotoDirect is heavier per image: a full-resolution encode at quality 90 capped only at WebP's 16383px dimension (actions.ts:345-350) — a ~90-100MP PNG scan is decoded twice (display + thumb) and q90-encoded at full size, which on one vCPU is plausibly 60-150s of CPU plus two 20MB transfers. Nothing in the repo sets maxDuration (no `export const maxDuration`, no functions block in vercel.json), so the ceiling is whatever the Vercel project's default is — 300s with Fluid compute, 60s on the legacy Hobby serverless default; the repo gives no evidence which applies. At 60s the collection path fails for exactly the archival scans the feature exists for; even at 300s the 3-file finalize plus a slow R2 day is uncomfortable. On timeout the member gets an opaque 504 after a long wait, and the staged original is left orphaned (ties to the staging-leak finding; the delete in `finally` never runs on a hard timeout).
findings.evidence: actions.ts:345-350: `const WEBP_MAX_DIM = 16383; const display = await sharpImage(original).rotate().resize(WEBP_MAX_DIM, WEBP_MAX_DIM, { fit: "inside", withoutEnlargement: true }).webp({ quality: 90 })...` followed by a second full decode for the thumb (line 355). image.ts:24 `MAX_INPUT_PIXELS = 100_000_000` — a 100MP encode at q90 is minutes-scale on serverless CPU. grep maxDuration across src and vercel.json: zero hits.
findings.fixDirection: Set an explicit `export const maxDuration` (e.g. 300) on /api/upload/finalize and confirm Fluid compute is enabled on the Vercel project (owner dashboard check); for contributePhotoDirect consider capping the display encode at a saner dimension (e.g. 8192px) or quality 82, and reuse the display decode for the thumb (resize from the decoded pipeline, not a second decode of the original).
findings.gateOrTest: Live timing test on production with a ~95MP, ~19MB PNG through the Collection contribute flow (test account), recording wall time; a comment/doc pinning the project's actual duration default.
findings.reproPlan: Test-account write via the app UI: contribute a synthetic 19MB ~95MP PNG to the Collection on production and time it; if it 504s, the finding is confirmed.

findings.title: Account export is unbounded (no take on any of the ten queries) and pretty-printed; a prolific member's export can exceed Vercel's 4.5MB response cap and 500
findings.expected: The GDPR export succeeds for the most prolific member the site can produce, or is chunked/streamed.
findings.actual: All ten findMany calls (posts, comments, likes, photos, catchupEntries, adminMessages, reportsFiled, contributions, places) have no `take`, everything is buffered into one object, and `JSON.stringify(body, null, 2)` roughly doubles the byte count with indentation before returning it as a single NextResponse. Vercel caps function response bodies at ~4.5MB; a member with years of letters (posts.content is the full text of every letter) plus hundreds of comments and catch-up answers can cross it, at which point the export 500s (FUNCTION_RESPONSE_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE) with no fallback — and the rate limit (3/day) means three failed attempts lock them out until tomorrow. Unlikely at launch, increasingly plausible over years toward the 2,000-member ceiling.
findings.evidence: export/route.ts:87-91 `prisma.post.findMany({ where: { authorId: userId }, orderBy: { createdAt: "asc" }, select: { ... content: true ... } })` — no take; line 164 `return new NextResponse(JSON.stringify(body, null, 2), ...)` — fully buffered, indented.
findings.fixDirection: Drop the pretty-printing (JSON.stringify(body)) to roughly halve the size now; longer-term, stream the JSON or split the export into sections. Optionally count bytes and, over a threshold, return a smaller non-indented body.
findings.gateOrTest: A unit test asserting the export uses compact JSON; a synthetic-data measurement of bytes-per-1000-posts to pin the real headroom.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only at current data volumes (fabricating a >4.5MB member on production would mean mass-writing real rows).

verifiedClean: 6f module-scope init: every third-party client is lazily constructed (S3Client via r2() in storage.ts:35, Upstash Redis via getRedis() in rate-limit.ts:104, Resend via resend() in email.ts:63, per-call PrismaClient in demo/reset); no top-level awaits anywhere in src/lib or src/app/api; Sentry is server-only via instrumentation.ts with enabled gating; the only import-time env throw is prisma.ts's DATABASE_URL check, which is fatal-anyway and set in all environments — CLEAN

6f build-time DB connections during static generation: the landing page and policy pages import no prisma; no generateStaticParams in the app tree; PrismaPg pool does not connect at construction — CLEAN

6g R2 1-write/sec-per-key: every putImage/presign key embeds a fresh cuid (uploads, collection, avatars, staging); avatar replacement writes a NEW key then deletes the old (settings/actions.ts:233,250), so no same-key overwrite path exists — CLEAN

6f response-size for the other endpoints: users-by-batch is capped at take:5000 of 5 small columns (~1MB worst case, audit H18); users/search and places/search take 8; all server-action list loaders paginate (PAGE_SIZE+1 pattern) — CLEAN except the account export reported above

6f duration for the bounded jobs: drainMailQueue is capped at BATCH=8 sends per pass inside after(); advanceDueCatchups is bounded by live editions with per-edition CAS transactions and createMany fanout (catchups-notify.ts:74, single-statement, no per-member loop); retention's table steps are single deleteMany statements; demo reset runs only on the demo deployment with a per-call client that is disconnected in finally — CLEAN at 2,000 users (the account-purge loop inside the sweep is the exception, reported)

6f after() usage where present is correctly structured: (main)/layout.tsx:63 drain, feed/actions.ts:180 collection copy, email-actions.ts:185 (audit L3), email-queue.ts scheduleDrain with the throws-outside-request fallback — CLEAN

6c proxy.ts per-request work: no DB, no fetch, synchronous FNV hash only; cron paths (/api/catchups/tick, /api/retention/sweep, /api/resend, /api/razorpay) are correctly on the public allowlist with in-route auth; the demo-closed lists match their in-route guards — CLEAN for this lens

6f/6i webhooks (resend, razorpay): raw-body HMAC over request.text(), small bodies, no loops-over-rows, replay window on resend; nothing that can exceed body or duration limits — CLEAN for the platform-limits lens

6g Sharp hardening: single sharpImage() wrapper with limitInputPixels=100MP, sequentialRead, failOn:'error' (audit M14) protects every attacker-supplied decode path; magic-byte sniff before decode everywhere — CLEAN as a decompression-bomb defence (worst-case DURATION on legitimate huge inputs reported separately)
6f streaming-then-error on API routes: all 14 routes buffer their responses (NextResponse.json / stringified body), none stream — CLEAN (page-level Suspense/streaming left to the React/Next agent)
coverageNotes: Read whole: vercel.json, next.config.ts, proxy.ts, all upload surfaces client and server (upload, presign, finalize routes; upload-client, image-downscale, upload-shared, storage, image libs; contribute-dialog, create-post-form upload section, message-composer, photo-attachments, avatar-crop-dialog callers in photo-step and letterhead-profile), email.ts + email-queue.ts, retention.ts + account-purge.ts + retention.yml, catchups.ts advance/notify halves + catchups-notify.ts, (main)/layout.tsx, prisma.ts, rate-limit.ts, login-attempt/search-log/content-view telemetry libs, account/export, users-by-batch, users/search, places/search, demo/reset, catchups/tick, retention/sweep routes, admin mail/people/profile-admin actions, collection actions + collection-intake, support actions, resend webhook (razorpay webhook skimmed for loops/body only). Skimmed only: dev-login and auth/[...nextauth] passthrough (trivial for this lens), demo-seed internals (demo-only blast radius), settings actions outside the avatar/audit regions. Consciously left to sibling agents: page-level Suspense/streaming and router-cache semantics (React/Next agent), N+1 and index coverage (scale agent), server-action race classes (concurrency agent), payment/webhook replay logic (payments agent). Duration-ceiling findings carry a stated uncertainty: no maxDuration is configured anywhere and the repo does not record whether the Vercel project runs Fluid compute (300s default) or legacy serverless (60s); the fix in both cases is an explicit maxDuration plus an owner dashboard check. Not re-reported per instructions: CRON_SECRET not yet set by the owner (tracked; note it currently 401s the two secret-gated crons nightly, leaving the lazy layout advance as the only catch-up driver — the finding on layout-blocking work is therefore live behaviour today), bugs.md items 2/3/5/5b/6/9/12-17, and the 2026-08-20 security-audit territory.
